title: Gus & Ilse
description: Gus Halvorsen buried his wife of 41 years three weeks ago. Closing her accounts, he found money going out every month that he had never seen. Her phone is still on the kitchen counter, and he needs someone to tell him who she was calling.

questions.question:

questions.hint: Check the recent calls in her Phone app.

Spot the same payee repeating at the start of every month.

questions.question:

What did my wife do?
answer: She killed Daniel in a hit-and-run
questions.hint: Back in Notes. Same lock as before.

Unlock it with 417, the same race bib number from the start-line photo.

Why: She writes that she was the driver in the hit-and-run that killed his father.

textSuccess:
Twenty-two years. She slept next to me every one of those nights and carried that by herself.

I keep thinking about the morning she came home and said she'd hit a deer. I went out and looked at the bumper. I said, "Could've been worse." God help me, I said that.

She didn't buy her way out of anything. She knew that. She just couldn't stop paying. Lunch every month, and the boy never knew why she was always there.

She called him first. Not me. I understand now. She wanted the last thing she did to be for him.

I'll go to Polly's on the first of the month. I'll sit in her seat. Then I'll do what she asked me to. I just need to find the words she couldn't.

onboardingContent.text: My wife died three weeks ago. A stroke, right there in our kitchen. I was at the hardware store buying a hinge. Her phone's been sitting on the counter since. I can't bring myself to move it.
That's my wife. Thirty years cleaning teeth in Eau Claire. Church every Sunday, crossword in pen, never wasted a dime. I'd have told you I knew every corner of her.
Closing her bank account, I found money going out every month. Years of it. Then the hospital told me she made one phone call before the ambulance came. It wasn't to me.
I'm no good with these phones. You are. Go through it for me, one thing at a time. Whatever's in there, I'd rather hear it from you than lie awake guessing.

Still scraping teeth, God help me. Dr. Petersen is cutting back to four days. We hired a young hygienist, sweet girl, but she doesn't know how you did the old schedule book.
😂 Paper and pencil, never failed me.
We're doing a little retirement potluck for Dolores at the end of the month. Would love to see you.
I wouldn't miss it. What's the date and what should I bring?
The 29th, noon, in the break room. Bring a dessert if you can.
Perfect. Seven-layer bars again?
PLEASE. People still talk about them.
Thanks for coming today! It was like old times. Dolores cried at the card.
I loved it. Please tell Dr. Petersen his new chairs are lovely. Still smells like fluoride varnish in there 😄
Some things never change. Would you ever want to sub for a few hours? We're desperate on Fridays.
Oh Karen, my license lapsed after I retired. And my wrists aren't what they were.
Had to ask! Worth a shot.
Quick question. My crown on the lower left has been sensitive to cold. Should I call or wait it out?
Call. Don't wait. I can squeeze you in Thursday morning if you want.
Thursday works. 9:30?
Booked. Don't eat ice cream before 😉
Just a little recession in the gum, nothing serious. Thanks for the fluoride trays!
Use them every night for two weeks. Bossy hygienist voice 😂
You can take the hygienist out of the office...
Do you remember Mr. Brekke who always brought us pickles from his garden?
Dill pickles in a Mason jar, every August! Of course.
His daughter dropped a jar off today. He passed in the spring. I cried at the front desk.
Oh Karen. He was a gentle man. Please give her my love.
I will. Anyway, lunch soon? My treat, there's a new soup place by the river.
I'd like that. Maybe in a couple weeks, things are busy at church right now.
No rush. Just don't disappear on me like last time 🙂
I promise. I'm bad at keeping in touch but I'm trying.
Soup place has a tomato basil that's supposed to be heaven. Thinking next week?
Let me check with Gus about the truck. Can I let you know in a couple days?
Of course!
Gus says yes, he'll manage on his own for an afternoon. How about the 15th?
The 15th! Perfect, I'll make a reservation for 12:30.
Ilse, did you get your garbage cart out? Truck came early.
Gus just wheeled it out. Thank you Marge!
Good. Last time the Hendersons' dog got into theirs and it was a mess.
My peonies are blooming. Come cut some for your table whenever.
Oh I'd love that. I'll come by after supper with scissors 🌸
Take as many as you like. The ants are a nuisance but the smell is worth it.
Have you seen the new people at the corner house? They've got a trampoline.
I saw it. Gus said the springs look rusty. He wanted to go over and look at them, I had to stop him.
😂 That man cannot see a machine without fixing it
Can I borrow your hedge trimmer? Mine died.
Sure. It's in the garage, Gus will bring it over. Be careful, it's got a mean kick.
He just brought it. He also sharpened the blade without being asked.
That's Gus.
Heads up, the city is paving our street next week. No parking on the south side.
Thank you for the warning. I'll tell Gus to move the truck into the drive.
Are you going to the block party on the 4th? Dennis is doing brats.
We'll watch from our back step this year. But I'll send over a pan of bars.
Seven-layer? You spoil us.
Whatever's left from the Circle meeting 😉
The brats were a hit. Dennis burned his thumb but he's proud.
We saw the fireworks from the step. The kids on Birch Street did a good show.
Your pan came back clean, thank you!
Something's been digging in my flower bed. Think it's a raccoon?
Could be skunks looking for grubs. Gus says sprinkle cayenne.
I'll try it. Thank you both.
Our power flickered about 3 a.m. Did yours?
Yes, the stove clock was blinking when I got up. Gus is resetting every clock in the house.
Mine too. Forty-one years in this house and I still can't set the oven clock.
I'm bringing you rhubarb crisp this afternoon. Tom's wife's recipe, but I fixed it.
I will be on the porch with a fork 😄
Dennis says thank you, he had two helpings.
That makes my day.
Ilse, the Sunday school fall schedule is out. Can you do the nursery rotation again?
I can do the first and third Sundays. Gus has his Packers game on the others 😉
The Packers aren't even playing in the spring, Ilse.
Don't tell him that.
Ha! Fine, first and third it is. Thank you.
We need volunteers for Vacation Bible School. Do you still have the felt board with the animals?
In the hall closet. The giraffe is missing a leg but the kids don't mind.
I'll swing by and get it this week. Thank you!
Picked up the felt board. Gus insisted on carrying it to my car even though it weighs nothing.
He's old school 🙂
He also fixed the squeak on my trunk lid. I didn't even ask.
That's how he says hello.
Can you help with snack at VBS? Goldfish crackers and juice, 25 kids.
Yes. I'll get the juice boxes at Festival Foods, they're buy-one-get-one this week.
You're a lifesaver.
VBS day one done. One kid threw up on the felt giraffe 😭
Oh no! I'll wash it at home. It can go on delicate.
Bless you. Tomorrow's craft is paper plate lambs.
I have cotton balls at home, I'll bring a whole bag.
VBS is finished. 31 kids by the end. Pastor was thrilled.
Wonderful. Those lambs were adorable.
Reminder: the church picnic is at Carson Park on the 26th. Sign up for potato salad or buns.
I'll do the potato salad. Mustard, not mayo, the way Gus likes.
Some of us like mayo, Ilse 😅
I'll make a small bowl of each.
You're too kind.
The sound system in the sanctuary is cutting out again. Could Gus take a look? Not asking, just wondering if he's up for it.
He'd be glad to. He's been bored since he got the garage organized. I'll bring him Sunday.
Wonderful! The tech volunteer is nineteen and keeps unplugging things at random.
Gus will love him. Or lecture him. Possibly both.
Hi Mrs. Halvorsen, Gary Nystrom Lawn Care. Starting the spring cleanup route. Can I come by this week?
Hello Gary. Yes please. Gus can't do the heavy raking anymore, though he'd never admit it.
Understood. I'll be there Thursday morning around 8.
Done! Cleaned the beds, hauled the branches. Invoice will come in the mail.
Looks beautiful. Thank you. Gus stood on the porch inspecting your edging.
Did he approve?
He said "Straight." That's an A+.
I'll take it 😄
Summer mowing schedule starts next week, every other week unless it's rainy. Same price as last year.
That's fine. Please skip the back strip by the fence, Gus likes to do that one himself.
Got it. Skipping the fence strip.
Mowed today. Noticed some brown patches near the maple. Could be grubs. Want me to treat?
Yes, please treat it. How much extra?
Thirty-five for the application. Safe for pets and kids.
Go ahead. Thank you.
Rain all day tomorrow, I'll push your mow to the day after.
No trouble. The grass will be glad for the rain.
Mowed. The patch near the maple is coming back green.
Good to hear. Gus is relieved. He was ready to dig up the whole thing.
Next mow is the 5th. Heads up the city is trimming trees on your block that week, could be some mess.
Thanks for the warning. Mow whenever works for you.
Mowed and swept the walk. The city crew left a pile of branches by your curb, I can haul it for a small fee.
The city usually picks those up. Let's wait a few days and see.
Sounds good. Let me know if they don't.
Morning Ilse. Are you still good for altar guild the first Sunday of April? Need to finalize the sheet.
Good morning Pastor. Yes, put me down. I'll bring the good linens, they came back from the cleaners.
Wonderful. Also, would you be willing to help with the Lenten soup supper again? Last year's split pea was a hit.
I can do the split pea and two loaves of bread. Gus will want to taste test, of course.
Ha! Tell Gus he's welcome to the first bowl.
Pastor, the food pantry shelf in the basement is nearly bare. Do you want me to pick up canned goods at Festival Foods on Thursday?
That would be a blessing. Keep the receipt and Pat in the office will reimburse you.
No need, it's my pleasure. I'll just drop it all at the side door.
Reminder: the church council meets tonight at 6:30. We're discussing the roof repair bids.
Thank you, Pastor. I'm not on council but I'll ask Gus to look at the bids. He knows his flashing from his shingles.
I would welcome his eye. Two of the bids look suspiciously low.
He says measure twice and never take the cheapest one. 😊
Sound advice. Thank you both. See you Sunday.
Pastor, can you add the Hendricks family to the prayer list? Their mother is in rehab after the hip surgery.
Of course, Ilse. I'll mention them Sunday. Thank you for always remembering.
Ilse! The tomatoes are going crazy this year. Want some? I can't give them away fast enough.
It's only May, Linda! 😄 Yours are early. Mine are barely up to my knee.
Greenhouse seedlings from the co-op. Worth every penny.
I'll walk over this afternoon and take a look. Gus wants to see your trellis anyway.
Come at 3, I'll have the coffee on.
Did you hear the Sandersons are selling their house? The sign went up this morning.
No! Forty years on this street. I'll miss seeing her wave from the porch.
Their son wants them closer to Madison. Makes sense I suppose.
We should bring a hotdish before they go.
Agreed. I'll do the bars if you do the hotdish.
Walk tomorrow morning? Seven, before it gets hot?
Seven is fine. My knee has been grumbling but I'll go slow.
Slow is my speed too. I'll meet you at the mailboxes.
Bringing you a bag of tomatoes and cucumbers on the way back.
You spoil us, Linda. Thank you.
Ilse, it's Judy. Got your number from Barb. Are you coming to the hygienists' reunion lunch?
Judy Olund! It's been ages. Where is it this year?
The Olive Garden by the mall. Eleven thirty on the 18th of June. Dr. Petersen's old crew is coming, even Marlene.
I wouldn't miss it. Marlene still owes me a story about the day the autoclave flooded the break room.
😂 She tells it better every year.
That was lovely. My cheeks hurt from laughing. Thank you for organizing.
Same here. We should do it twice a year instead of once.
Fall then. I'll start asking around in September.
Hey, quick question. Who did you see for your crown after you left the practice? My new dentist is rough.
Dr. Haugen on Clairemont. Gentle hands and he actually numbs you properly.
Perfect, I'll call tomorrow. Thank you!
Went to Dr. Haugen. You were right. No jaw ache at all.
Told you. Old hygienist knows best. 😊
How's Gus? Still out in the garage every day?
Every day. He's rebuilding a lathe someone gave him. My wife is a patient woman, he says. I say he has no choice.
Bob's Plumbing & Heating here. Confirming your furnace tune-up for Thursday between 9 and 11.
Thank you, that works. Please use the side door, the front steps are icy.
Will do. Our tech Kyle will call 20 minutes before arriving.
Thanks for having us. Your furnace is in good shape. Filter replaced. Invoice sent to your email.
Received, thank you. Gus says the pilot assembly looked fine to him too. 😄
Ha, tell him he's welcome to apply.
Hello, the basement has a small puddle near the sump pump after last night's rain. Could someone come look?
Sorry to hear that. We can send someone tomorrow morning around 8:30. Does that work?
Yes please. Gus will be home.
Tech found the float switch stuck. Replaced it, tested it. Pump is running fine now.
Wonderful. Thank you for coming so fast.
Reminder: our annual water heater flush special is running through the end of July. Reply YES to schedule.
YES
Great! We have an opening on the 22nd of September at 10 AM. Should we book it?
That works, thank you.

notes.title: For Gus
notes.content:
Gus,

I have started this note four times and deleted it three. You know I can't say hard things out loud. You'd put your hand on the back of my chair and I'd lose my nerve.

There is something I have carried since before you and I were old. I let you believe a small thing so you wouldn't ask about a big thing, and then the years went by. Every month I tried to make some of it right, and it was never enough.

There is a young man. You've never met him, but you would like him. He has your way of fixing a thing instead of talking about it. He doesn't know what I owe him, and he needs to hear it from someone steadier than I am.

I couldn't do it to his face, and I ran out of time to be brave. You were always the brave one.

Please, my love — tell him.

I. ❤️

notes.title: Jonah
notes.content:
Jonah,

I was the driver. The hit-and-run on Mill Creek Road that took your father — it was me. I didn't stop. I have never stopped being sorry.

I fixed the car in another town and told my husband it was a deer. I told myself that was the end of it. It wasn't. Eleven years later I asked to be paired with you, and I told myself that was for you. Mostly it was.

The tuition was never charity. It was never enough, either. Nothing I could pay would be.

You don't have to forgive me. You don't have to answer. I only didn't want you to find out from a stranger or a newspaper.

You are going to be a fine nurse. Gentle hands. Take care of your mother.

Ilse

messages.content: what is the statute of limitations in Wisconsin if someone died in an accident and the driver left

I'm sorry, that sounds like a heavy thing to be thinking about at this hour. Here is the general picture, though I'm not a lawyer and the details matter a great deal.

In Wisconsin, the statute of limitations depends on the specific crime charged. Many felonies have a time limit, but the most serious homicide offenses have none at all. Some other rules can also pause the clock, for example if the person was out of state for a period.

Because the answer depends on exactly which offense applies, a Wisconsin criminal defense attorney is the right person to ask. Many offer a confidential first consultation.
and if it was 20 years ago

Twenty years is a long time, but it doesn't automatically mean the statute of limitations has run out. It depends on the charge, and the most serious charges have no deadline. I can't say how it would apply to a specific situation. An attorney could tell you, and they are bound to keep what you say private.
is there still a statute of limitations after 20 years

It depends on the offense. Some crimes have a statute of limitations that expires after a set number of years. Others, the most serious ones, can be charged at any time. In Wisconsin the time limit can also be extended in certain circumstances.

I can't tell you which category a particular case falls into. A criminal defense attorney can review the facts in confidence and give you a real answer.
if someone came forward on their own does that change anything

Coming forward voluntarily doesn't erase a charge, but prosecutors and judges often take it into account. Cooperation and honesty can matter at charging, at sentencing, and in how a family experiences the outcome. It's worth speaking to an attorney before making any statement, so you understand your options first.
thank you

- Don't ask them to comfort you or to decide right away.
- Give them time and space to react however they react.
- If saying it aloud feels impossible, a letter can be a fair way to begin, as long as you follow it with a conversation.

My mother's lefse recipe says to rice the potatoes but my ricer broke. Can I mash them instead?

You can, but the texture matters a lot for lefse. Lumps make the dough tear when you roll it thin.

Options, best to worst:
1. A food mill, if you have one.
2. A potato masher, then press the potatoes through a fine mesh strainer.
3. A hand masher alone. Mash while the potatoes are still very hot and keep going until there are no lumps at all.

Whatever you use, let the potatoes cool completely before adding flour.
How much flour per cup of potatoes? Her card just says 'enough'

A common ratio is about 1/2 cup of flour for every 1 cup of packed riced potatoes. Many recipes add a little butter, cream and salt as well.

Start with less flour and add it a spoonful at a time. The dough should be soft and just barely sticky. More flour makes the lefse tough.
It's sticking to my pastry cloth something awful

Sticking is usually one of three things:
- The dough is too warm. Chill it for at least an hour, or overnight.
- The cloth needs flour. Rub flour into the cloth and onto the rolling pin cover, then knock off the excess.
- The dough is too wet. Work in a little more flour.

Roll from the center outward and lift the dough often to check it.
Chilling it helped. Now what temperature for the griddle?

Around 450–500°F on an electric lefse griddle. On a stovetop skillet, use medium-high heat with no oil.

Cook about 30–60 seconds per side. You want light brown freckles, not dark spots. Stack the finished rounds between clean towels so they stay soft.

The leaves on my hydrangea by the back porch are getting brown crispy edges. It's in Wisconsin, gets afternoon sun. What's wrong?

Brown, crispy edges on hydrangea leaves are most often caused by:

1. Too much afternoon sun. Hydrangeas prefer morning sun and afternoon shade.
2. Uneven watering. They have shallow roots and dry out quickly.
3. Late frost damage on new growth, which is common in Wisconsin in spring.
4. Too much fertilizer, which can burn the leaf edges.

How long has it been happening, and did it get a hard frost this spring?
We had a frost in mid May after it leafed out. It's only the older leaves on the south side.

That points to frost damage combined with sun stress on the south side. The plant will probably recover on its own.

What to do:
- Leave it alone. New growth will come in green.
- Water deeply two or three times a week if it's dry, at the base rather than on the leaves.
- Spread 2–3 inches of mulch to hold moisture.
- Skip fertilizer until the plant looks healthy again.

Don't prune it hard now. If it's a bigleaf type, you could remove next year's flower buds.
Should I move it? Gus says leave it, he doesn't want to dig.

Gus has a point. Moving a mature hydrangea in summer stresses it badly. If you still want to move it, wait until early fall or early spring, when it's cool and the plant is dormant or nearly so.

For now, a shade cloth or a tall pot of something leafy on the south side could cut the afternoon sun.
The blooms were blue last year and pinkish this year. Why?

Bloom color in bigleaf hydrangeas depends on soil pH and aluminum availability.
- Acidic soil (pH below about 5.5) gives blue flowers.
- Neutral to alkaline soil gives pink.

Heavy rain, lime from a nearby walkway or foundation, or changes in fertilizer can shift the color. To push it back to blue, use aluminum sulfate according to the package directions, applied in spring.
I did put some wood ash from the burn barrel around it last fall. That explains it.
Yes, wood ash is alkaline and would raise the pH. That's very likely the cause. Keep ash away from it and the color should drift back toward blue over a season or two.
Pink is fine too. Thanks.
I got a letter that says 'Explanation of Benefits - This is not a bill.' It lists a charge of $312 and then 'You may be billed $0.00'. Do I owe anything?

If the letter says 'This is not a bill' and 'You may be billed $0.00', you most likely owe nothing for that service.

The usual breakdown on an Explanation of Benefits is:
- Amount billed: what the provider charged ($312 here)
- Amount approved: what Medicare or your plan agreed to pay
- Plan paid: what the insurer covered
- You may owe: your share, which here is $0.00

You only owe money when you receive an actual bill from the provider. Compare any bill to this letter.
What does 'deductible' mean on it? There's a line with $240 next to it.

The deductible is the amount you pay yourself each year before insurance starts paying. If a line shows $240 applied to your deductible, that part of the charge counted toward what you must pay out of pocket first.

If the final line still shows $0.00 owed, it likely means your supplement plan covered that deductible. Check the column labeled 'Other insurance' or 'Supplement paid'.
There is a column like that. It says paid in full. So I'm fine?

That looks right. 'Paid in full' by the supplement means you shouldn't owe the provider anything for this claim.

Keep the letter with your records for a year or so. If a bill later arrives for this service, call the Medicare number on the back of your card or the provider's billing office and ask them to check the claim.
Also there's a phone number in the letter for a 'Medicare Summary Notice'. Is that a scam?

A Medicare Summary Notice is real. Medicare mails them every three months. But scammers do copy them.

Safe habits:
- Don't call numbers from a letter or text you aren't sure of. Use the number on your Medicare card, 1-800-MEDICARE.
- Medicare will never call to ask for your card number or bank information.
- You can check your claims by logging in to the official Medicare website.
I'll call the number on my card tomorrow. Thank you, this was clear.
My HP printer says 'offline' and I can't print from my phone. It worked last week. What do I do?

Printers often show 'offline' after a router restart or power flicker. Try these steps in order:

1. Turn the printer off, unplug it for 30 seconds, then plug it in again.
2. Check the wireless light or the wifi icon on the printer screen. A steady light means it's connected.
3. Make sure your phone is on the same wifi network as the printer.
4. Restart your phone's wifi.

Does the printer have a screen?
It has a small screen. A little wifi symbol is blinking.

A blinking wifi symbol usually means the printer lost its connection and is searching for your network.

On the printer screen:
1. Open Setup or the wireless icon.
2. Choose Wireless Settings, then Wireless Setup Wizard.
3. Select your home network from the list.
4. Enter your wifi password.

The password is often printed on a sticker on the router.
It found two networks with almost the same name. One ends in 5G.

Many older printers only work on the 2.4 GHz network. The one ending in 5G is the faster 5 GHz band, and some printers can't connect to it.

Choose the name without 5G. The password is usually the same for both.
That did it, the symbol is steady now. My phone still doesn't see it though.

Good. Now on your phone:
1. Open whatever you're printing from (Photos, a PDF, an email) and choose Share, then Print.
2. Tap Select Printer and wait a few seconds.
3. If it doesn't appear, check that the phone is on the same network as the printer, the one without 5G.

If it still isn't listed, install the printer manufacturer's free app and add the printer there.
My phone was on the 5G one. Switched it and the printer showed up.

That was the problem. Your phone and printer were on different bands. You should be able to print now. Next time it goes offline, restarting the printer and checking both devices are on the same network will usually fix it.
Printed the church bulletin test page. Works. Thanks.
I'm making a quilt top that measures 64 by 80 inches. How much backing fabric do I need? The fabric is 44 inches wide.

For a quilt top of 64 x 80 inches, add at least 4 inches on every side for the quilting machine or for shifting while you quilt. Your backing should be at least 72 x 88 inches.

With 44-inch fabric, one width isn't enough, so you'll need to piece two lengths together.

- Run the seam along the 88-inch direction.
- Two widths of 44 inches give 88 inches across (before seam allowances).
- Each piece is 72 inches long, or 2 yards.

So you need about 4 yards, plus a little extra for seam allowances and shrinkage. Buying 4¼ yards is safer.
Wait, 88 across? The quilt is only 64 wide.

You're right to question that, and I laid it out confusingly. Here's the corrected version.

The backing needs to be 72 inches wide and 88 inches long. Two 44-inch widths sewn together make about 86–87 inches once you subtract seam allowances. That's not wide enough for 72 only if you were running the seam the wrong way.

Cleanest way: cut two pieces, each 44 inches wide by 88 inches long, and sew them side by side along the long edge. That gives you about 86 inches wide by 88 long. That's more than the 72 you need.

That approach takes 2 x 88 inches = 176 inches, about 4⅞ yards. So buy 5 yards.

A cheaper way: cut one length of 80 inches and one of 80, seam them across the 64-inch direction, and the pieced backing will cover 88 inches in that direction. Then you need 2 x 72 = 144 inches, or 4 yards, plus extra, so buy 4¼ yards. That is the layout from my first answer, with the seam running across the quilt's width.
That's a lot of words. So 4 and a quarter yards is enough?

Yes. 4¼ yards is enough if you cut two pieces 72 inches long, trim the selvages, and sew them together along the long edges. After the seam you'll have about 86 inches of width, which covers your 80-inch quilt length plus the 4 inches on each side.

Sorry for the confusion. Short version: buy 4¼ yards, cut it in half, sew the halves together, and trim to size.
Good. Should I wash the fabric first? Marge says never, Dorothy says always.

Both are common opinions, and both can work.

Pre-wash if:
- the fabric is deep red, navy, or another color that might bleed
- you'll mix it with other fabrics that have different shrinkage
- you plan to wash the finished quilt often

Skip pre-washing if:
- you want the crinkled look after the first wash
- you're using pre-cut pieces that could fray

For backing, many quilters pre-wash, since a big piece shrinking later can pucker the quilt. Use a color catcher sheet in the first wash, then press it well.

Ha, I'll leave that to you. Enjoy the quilt. Cream with small blue flowers will look lovely.

**Prep:** 1 hour | **Cook:** 30 minutes | **Makes:** 16 rounds

## Ingredients
- 4 cups riced potatoes, cold
- 1/4 cup real butter
- 1/4 cup heavy cream
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 1/2 cups flour

2. Work in the flour a little at a time.
3. Roll each round paper thin on a floured cloth.
4. Cook on a hot griddle until pale brown spots appear, about a minute per side.

# Stroke Warning Signs
**Healthy Seniors Guide — Know the signs, act fast**

---

## Remember F.A.S.T.

- **F — Face drooping.** Does one side of the face droop or feel numb?
- **A — Arm weakness.** Is one arm weak or numb? Does it drift downward when raised?
- **S — Speech difficulty.** Is speech slurred or hard to understand?
- **T — Time to call 911.** Call right away, even if the symptoms go away.

## Other sudden symptoms
- Trouble seeing in one or both eyes
- Sudden severe headache with no known cause
- Dizziness or loss of balance
- Confusion

> Note the time the first symptoms started. Doctors will ask.

## Who is at higher risk?
High blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, and a family history of stroke all raise risk. Talk with your doctor about a screening plan.

*Digitized from the print edition. Originally published September 2004.*

EAU CLAIRE — A 33-year-old Eau Claire man died early yesterday morning after he was struck by a vehicle while riding his bicycle on a county road north of the city. The driver did not stop.

The man, whose name is being withheld pending notification of family, was pronounced dead at the scene. A passing motorist found him on the shoulder shortly after sunrise and called for help.

The Eau Claire County Sheriff's Office said deputies are asking anyone who was on county roads north of the city in the early morning hours to come forward. Investigators are examining debris found at the scene.

---

EAU CLAIRE — Twenty years ago this month, a man on a morning ride never came home.

Daniel Whitcombe, 33, was struck while cycling on Mill Creek Road just after 6 a.m. The driver kept going. Whitcombe, an electrician and a familiar face at weekend charity rides, died at the scene.

He left behind a wife, Carla, and a young son, Jonah.

"Every year I drive that road once," a former neighbor said. "I slow down at the same spot. I don't know why. It just feels like the right thing to do."

The case has never been solved. Investigators have never released a vehicle description publicly, and the Eau Claire County Sheriff's Office says the file remains open.

> "Somebody out there knows," a sheriff's spokesperson said. "Twenty years is a long time to carry something. It is never too late to call."

A small memorial ride is planned for this weekend, starting at the Chippewa Valley fairgrounds.

safariTabs.content:
# Classic Tater Tot Hotdish
**Midwest Comfort Cooking**

*Prep: 15 min | Cook: 55 min | Serves: 8*

No church basement potluck is complete without a hotdish. This one has been feeding Minnesota and Wisconsin families for generations.

---

## Ingredients

- 1 1/2 lb lean ground beef
- 1 small yellow onion, chopped
- 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup
- 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of celery soup
- 1/2 cup milk
- 1 bag (16 oz) frozen green beans
- 1 bag (32 oz) frozen tater tots
- 1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar
- Salt and pepper to taste

## Directions

1. Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a 9x13 pan.
2. Brown beef and onion in a skillet, drain.
3. Stir in soups and milk. Fold in green beans.
4. Spread in the pan and cover with cheese.
5. Arrange tater tots in rows on top.
6. Bake 50–55 minutes until golden and bubbly.

> **Tip:** Cover with foil if you're carrying it to a potluck. It stays warm for an hour.

### Reader Comments

**Bev K.:** Made this for our Lutheran Women's Circle luncheon. Gone in ten minutes!

**Ron T.:** My wife swears by adding a little Worcestershire.

safariTabs.title: Planting Spring Bulbs in Wisconsin - UW Extension
safariTabs.content:
# Planting Spring Bulbs in Wisconsin
**University of Wisconsin–Madison Division of Extension**

---

## When to Plant

Plant tulips, daffodils, crocus and hyacinths in the fall, once soil temperatures drop below **60°F**. In northern Wisconsin, that usually means late September through mid-October. Aim to get bulbs in the ground at least six weeks before the ground freezes.

## How Deep?

A good rule: plant bulbs **two to three times as deep as the bulb is tall**.

| Bulb | Depth | Spacing |
|---|---|---|
| Tulip | 6–8 in | 4–6 in |
| Daffodil | 6 in | 6 in |
| Crocus | 3–4 in | 3 in |
| Hyacinth | 6 in | 5 in |

## Protect from Critters

Squirrels and chipmunks love tulip bulbs. Daffodils are poisonous to them and make a good companion planting. Chicken wire laid over the bed and covered with mulch also works.

## Soil

Bulbs rot in soggy ground. Choose a spot with well-drained soil and at least six hours of sun in spring.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Do I need to fertilize?** A little bone meal or a balanced bulb fertilizer at planting time is plenty.

**Should I water after planting?** Yes, one good soaking helps roots get started.

## Declaration of Trust

## Article 1 — Name and Establishment

This trust shall be known as the **Larkspur Scholarship Fund** ("LSF"), established in August 2022 as an irrevocable charitable trust under the laws of the State of Wisconsin.

## Article 2 — Purpose

The purpose of the Fund is tuition support for one named student in the nursing program of an accredited Wisconsin college, until the student completes the degree.

## Article 3 — Funding

The Fund shall be supported by a fixed monthly contribution of $400.00, received on the first day of each month by electronic transfer into the trust account ending 2281.

## Article 4 — Disbursement

The Trustee shall pay tuition and required fees directly to the college bursar each term. No funds shall be paid to the student in cash.

## Article 5 — Confidentiality

The identity of the Grantor shall remain confidential. The Trustee shall not disclose the Grantor to the student, the college, or any third party.

## Article 6 — Reports

The Trustee shall issue an annual statement to the Grantor each spring.
